whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Public Sector Solutions AP exam for?

personas.label: Public agency implementers
personas.description: You build Salesforce services for local, state, or national government and want to demonstrate your Public Sector Solutions knowledge.

personas.label: Government consultants and admins
personas.description: You configure licence, permit, grant, or benefits processes and want a credential that reflects this work.

personas.label: Salesforce professionals entering government
personas.description: You know the Salesforce platform and want to apply those skills in the public sector.

examDifficulty.heading: How difficult is the Public Sector Solutions AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: Expect a moderate exam about government processes. Public Sector Solutions includes tools for licences, permits, inspections, grants, and benefits, with records for each process. Questions ask you to match an agency need to the appropriate process or record.
bullets: 60 multiple-choice questions with 90 minutes to answer.
About 65% to pass, or around 39 correct answers. Verify the current score in the official exam guide.
Government processes. Review licensing, inspections, grants, benefits, and case management.
Implementation tools. OmniStudio supports guided forms and steps; Experience Cloud supports constituent portals.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before the exam, follow a licence request from submission through review, approval, and inspection in a trial org. Aim for at least 75% on practice questions before booking.

examFormat.heading: Public Sector Solutions AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are delivered online. Prepare for questions like these:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe an agency task, such as granting a food business licence or paying a grant, and ask which feature or record supports it.
bestWayToPass: Study the process records: Learn which records support licences, inspections, grants, and benefits and how they relate.
Trace an application: Follow it from public intake through review and approval to a licence or award.
Understand OmniStudio: Review how guided steps, intake forms, and data lookups use its tools.
Consider the constituent journey: Know how self-service, status updates, and accessible forms help the public.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers configuring Public Sector Solutions for licensing and permitting, inspections, grants, benefits, case management, and constituent self-service.

keyConcepts.h2: Public Sector Solutions AP concepts to review

blocks.heading: Government case management
blocks.body: Agencies use cases to manage complaints, investigations, and service requests. Public Sector Solutions extends Service Cloud case management with government-focused records such as interviews and investigations, and helps track the people and organizations involved. Teams can route cases to the right staff, connect them to licences or inspections, and monitor deadlines. Restrict access when a case contains sensitive information.

blocks.heading: Licences and permits
blocks.body: People and businesses apply for licences and permits, such as food service approval or a building permit. A regulatory authorization type defines a licence or permit and its rules. An application is submitted, often through a public portal, and then reviewed for checks, fees, and approvals. Once approved, the licence record includes an expiry date. Applicants can view the application status online, and renewals can use a similar process.

blocks.heading: Grant funding
blocks.body: Grant programs use funding opportunities to describe available funds and eligibility. Organizations submit applications for review and scoring. If approved, an application becomes an award with a budget and conditions. Disbursements record payments, which may depend on milestones or grantee reports. These records help agencies track how public funds are awarded and spent.

blocks.heading: Inspections and compliance
blocks.body: Inspectors visit locations to check requirements, such as restaurant hygiene or building safety. A planned visit can include assessment tasks for the inspector to complete, including on a mobile device. The result may pass, fail, or require follow-up. A failed check can create a violation and enforcement action, with another inspection scheduled as needed. The inspection connects to the business and its licence.

blocks.heading: Digital service for constituents
blocks.body: People expect to apply, pay, and check progress online. Experience Cloud portals allow constituents to submit applications, provide documents, and follow status. OmniStudio can power the forms: OmniScripts guide users through steps, while Integration Procedures and Data Mappers retrieve and save information. Forms should be accessible and usable on phones. Government Cloud is designed for public sector security standards.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Public Sector Solutions AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: First identify the agency process in the question: licensing, inspection, grants, benefits, or cases. Then select the record or feature that supports that process.

blocks.heading: Know the public sector records
blocks.body: Licensing uses authorization types and applications; grants use opportunities, applications, and awards; inspections use visits and assessments.

blocks.heading: Follow the grant lifecycle
blocks.body: A funding opportunity leads to an application, review, and award. Disbursements record payments, which may depend on milestones.

blocks.heading: Understand licensing
blocks.body: Regulatory authorization types define licence rules. Applications pass through review before an issued licence receives an expiry date.

blocks.heading: Support constituent self-service
blocks.body: Portals help people apply, pay, and check status. Staff can review the related history in Salesforce.

blocks.heading: Use OmniStudio appropriately
blocks.body: OmniScripts guide people through forms. Integration Procedures can retrieve data from other systems.

sampleQuestions.question: A city wants local businesses to apply for food licences online and follow their applications. What should the agency configure?
options: A licence application process with an online public form
A visit for inspectors only
A funding opportunity for grants
A separate marketing campaign and landing page for each business
sampleQuestions.explanation: Licensing and permitting manages applications, review, and issuing licences. A portal lets applicants submit requests and check progress.
whyWrong: Inspection visits are used to check compliance, often after a licence is issued.
Grant opportunities support funding, not licence applications.
Campaigns are marketing records, not a licensing process.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should an agency define the rules for a particular licence, such as a liquor licence?
options: A dashboard
A regulatory authorization type
A case queue
A grant funding opportunity record
sampleQuestions.explanation: A regulatory authorization type defines a licence or permit category and its rules.
whyWrong: Dashboards display data but do not define licence rules.
Queues route work to users; they do not define a licence type.
Funding opportunities describe grants.

sampleQuestions.question: An inspector needs to visit a restaurant and complete a hygiene checklist on a tablet. What should the agency use?
options: An inspection visit with assessment tasks
A licence renewal
A grant application with an attached document checklist
A Chatter post
sampleQuestions.explanation: An inspection visit can include assessment tasks that an inspector completes in the field.
whyWrong: A renewal extends an existing licence.
Grant applications request funding.
Chatter is for collaboration, not tracking inspections.

sampleQuestions.question: A restaurant does not pass its hygiene inspection. What is an appropriate next step?
options: Close the business account
Record a violation and plan a follow-up inspection
Delete the inspection record and schedule nothing further
Issue another licence
sampleQuestions.explanation: A failed assessment can result in a violation and a repeat inspection, linked to the business and its licence.
whyWrong: Closing an account is not how an inspection failure is recorded.
A failed visit should remain in the record for history.
A failed inspection does not justify issuing another licence.

sampleQuestions.question: A state agency is offering $2 million in community grants. Where should it describe the program and eligibility?
options: A funding opportunity
A benefits enrollment
An inspection visit
A regulatory authorization type
sampleQuestions.explanation: A funding opportunity describes a grant program, including what is offered and who may apply.
whyWrong: Benefit enrollment is for people receiving benefits.
Inspection visits record compliance checks.
Authorization types define licences and permits.

sampleQuestions.question: A grant award should be paid in three installments as the recipient meets milestones. Which record supports these payments?
options: One payment made before any milestones
A violation record
Disbursements connected to milestones
A licence renewal
sampleQuestions.explanation: Disbursements record grant payments and can be tied to milestones or reports.
whyWrong: A single advance payment would not represent the requested staged payments.
Violations track failed compliance checks.
Licence renewals are unrelated to grant payments.

sampleQuestions.question: A review panel must score grant applications before deciding which to fund. What should the agency use?
options: A dashboard of applications that each reviewer reads on their own
A structured application review with reviewers and scores
An email inbox
A licence type
sampleQuestions.explanation: The grants process supports application reviews in which assigned reviewers can score submissions.
whyWrong: A dashboard presents information but does not conduct a review.
An inbox does not provide a structured scoring process.
Licence types support licensing, not grant review.

sampleQuestions.question: A public intake form has several steps and must retrieve information from another government system. Which tools fit?
options: A Campaign
A report
An OmniScript with an Integration Procedure
A long text field on the application for pasted details
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScripts guide a person through steps. Integration Procedures can retrieve data from another system.
whyWrong: Campaigns are used for marketing.
Reports show existing data rather than guiding an intake flow.
A text field cannot guide a multi-step form or retrieve external data.

sampleQuestions.question: A complaint investigation requires interviews with several people. Which Public Sector Solutions area supports this work?
options: Case management with investigation and interview features
Grant management
Loyalty management
Licensing and permitting, with a new licence type for each interview
sampleQuestions.explanation: Government case management includes support for investigations and interviews.
whyWrong: Grant management handles public funding.
Loyalty tools are not designed for complaint investigations.
Licensing issues permits and licences.

sampleQuestions.question: A licence expires every year. How should the agency process a renewal?
options: Require applicants to call by phone only
Manually change the expiry date every year
Delete the licence record and create a replacement each year
Use a renewal application linked to the current licence
sampleQuestions.explanation: The renewal can follow an application process and remain linked to the existing licence for a clear history.
whyWrong: Phone-only handling is difficult to track and does not provide the online process.
Changing a date manually can skip required checks or fees.
Deleting and recreating the record loses the licence history.

sampleQuestions.question: An agency needs its Salesforce environment to meet public sector security requirements. What should it evaluate?
options: Public Read/Write record access
A shared administrator login
A Developer Edition org
Government Cloud
sampleQuestions.explanation: Government Cloud is designed to meet public sector security and compliance requirements.
whyWrong: Public sharing can expose records beyond the intended audience.
Shared logins make it difficult to know who performed an action.
Developer Edition is intended for development and testing.

sampleQuestions.question: A complaint concerns a licensed business that also failed an inspection. Why connect the related records?
options: To hide the failed inspection
To remove the complaint from the system once the inspection closes
To let staff review the business history together
To raise the business’s licence fee
sampleQuestions.explanation: Related records give staff a fuller view of the business and help them make informed decisions.
whyWrong: Linking records does not hide the inspection.
A relationship does not remove the complaint.
Fees depend on licence rules, not on linking records.

sampleQuestions.question: Constituents need to upload documents and check application status from a phone. What design best supports this?
options: Accepting documents only by postal mail
An accessible Experience Cloud portal designed for mobile use
Hiding the application status until a final decision has been reached
Requiring everyone to use a desktop computer
sampleQuestions.explanation: An accessible, mobile-friendly portal lets constituents send documents and follow progress on their phones.
whyWrong: Postal mail alone does not meet the mobile self-service need.
Visible status helps people understand where their application stands.
A desktop-only service excludes people who rely on phones.

sampleQuestions.question: Only the investigations team should see sensitive investigation cases. How should access be configured?
options: Use a Chatter group to control case access
Set organization-wide defaults to Public Read Only for all Case records
Keep sharing private and grant access to the investigation team
Give every user View All access
sampleQuestions.explanation: Private sharing with access granted to the investigation team limits visibility to the appropriate staff.
whyWrong: A Chatter group does not set record access.
Public Read Only exposes records to all users.
View All gives everyone broad access.

sampleQuestions.question: Which records represent the core grants lifecycle?
options: Campaign and campaign member
Lead, opportunity, and quote
Inspection visit, assessment task, violation, and regulatory code
Funding opportunity, application, award, and disbursements
sampleQuestions.explanation: The process starts with the funding offered, continues through applications and awards, and records payments as disbursements.
whyWrong: Campaign records support marketing.
Leads, opportunities, and quotes are part of sales work.
Visits and assessment tasks support inspections.
